source.title: LedgerCloud changes its pricing
source.article: LedgerCloud will replace its $20 monthly developer plan with a $5 base fee plus $1 per thousand API calls on November 1. The company says 60% of current accounts make fewer than 10,000 calls a month. Existing annual contracts keep their price until renewal. Usage alerts arrive at 80% of a customer-set budget; they do not stop requests. Customers can set a hard cap, which rejects excess requests.

comments.author: fixture_author_201
comments.text: My integration retries failed requests. If those count as billable calls, an outage could increase my bill. I cannot find a definition of a billable call.

comments.author: fixture_author_202
comments.text: A hard cap would stop that bill but could also take checkout offline. The cap policy has to match how critical the integration is.

topics.title: Retry billing remains undefined
topics.summary: Failed requests that retry may count as billable calls, and the definition of a billable call remains unclear, leaving outage costs uncertain.

topics.title: Hard caps can halt checkout
topics.summary: A hard cap prevents runaway bills but rejects excess requests, so it can take checkout offline; the cap policy must match integration criticality.

source.title: Helio ships a smaller model build
source.article: Helio released a quantized build of its language model on Friday. In Helio's batch-one test, GPU memory fell from 32GB to 20GB, while throughput fell from 130 to 110 tokens per second. The test used one A100 GPU and English prompts. The weights are available under Apache 2.0.

comments.author: new_reader_701
comments.text: Fitting within a 24GB card can matter more than losing some throughput if the alternative is buying a larger card. This test alone does not establish performance on a different GPU.

comments.author: new_reader_702
comments.text: I tested ten French prompts and noticed worse answers. That tiny sample is not enough to measure an accuracy regression.
